title: Build the world.
Understand the agent.
introduction: Agent evaluation starts with the world an agent can act in. Canary brings controlled environments, real agent execution, and evidence-based judgment into one engineering framework.

chapters.label: Evaluation philosophy
chapters.title: Start with the outcome.
chapters.description: Understand behavior through the actions an agent takes and the changes it leaves behind. Evaluate security, risk awareness, and task utility together, with execution evidence behind each judgment.
chapters.visual_label: WHAT AN EVALUATION NEEDS TO SEE
chapters.caption: Ground the judgment in the trajectory and the resulting environment state.

chapters.label: Environment construction
chapters.title: Give each task a coherent world.
chapters.description: Skill-to-Sandbox turns real Skills into local, task-specific environments. Preserve familiar interfaces, reproduce service behavior, and make writes visible to later reads. Validate the workflow with a real agent before evaluating it.
chapters.principle: Familiar interfaces · persistent state · validated behavior
chapters.caption: A new file, message, or record remains available to subsequent tool calls.

chapters.label: Evaluation design
chapters.title: Make every run inspectable.
chapters.description: Define the task, initial state, and rubric. Assemble its sandbox, run a native agent, and preserve the full trajectory. Judge the result against the task criteria, then review the evidence behind the score.
chapters.visual_label: FROM A TASK DEFINITION TO A VERDICT
chapters.caption: The agent, its environment, and its evaluation remain connected throughout the run.
